# SEV-1 INCIDENT - RELEASE BLOCKER
**Title:** Statements are filing some payments under the wrong kind of transaction, or dropping the payee name
**Owner:** Payments Operations
**Disposition:** Do not ship this release until it is resolved

## What customers reported

Over the past few days support has collected a run of tickets that all share one
shape: the money itself moved fine, but the app files the payment under a category
that does not match what the customer actually did, or shows the wrong name - or
no name at all - beside it. In every case the row that misbehaves carries one very
particular, uncommon form of raw statement text; everyday rows are labeled exactly
as before. The tickets below are anonymized, but the raw narration each customer
pasted is reproduced verbatim, because that raw text is what makes each case
reproducible.

> "I wrote a cheque against my account and the app just lists it as a general
> transfer now - nothing marks it as a cheque anymore. My earlier cheques were
> tagged correctly. The only thing sitting in that row's note is the cheque's own
> number, nothing else around it."

> "My salary came in and the amount is right, but where my employer's name should
> be the app now just prints the word `NACH`. The raw text on that row looks like
> `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` - it used to lift the employer's name off the end
> of that reference, and now it is picking up the wrong piece of it."

> "On some transfers that come in, the sender's name is blank now. Those rows all
> share the same reference layout - a short block of letters, then a long string
> of digits, then the name - for example `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`. The name
> sitting at the end just is not being pulled through anymore; the name column
> comes out empty."

The same batch of complaints also covers two quieter cases that are about the
category rather than the name. The token confirmation charge a bank posts when a
new auto-debit mandate is set up - a small nominal amount, with the note flagging
it as a mandate - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being
recognized as a verification entry. And a refund that came back on a card is
landing as a plain refund for some customers when it should read as a card
reversal; a customer on a different type of account sees the same kind of refund
labeled correctly, so the wrong label appears to depend on the account category.

## Scope of impact

Everyday activity - normal purchases, routine transfers, regular deposits - is
categorized and named correctly, which is precisely why this slipped through QA and
why our monitoring dashboards looked healthy. The breakage is confined to a small
set of unusual transaction forms - among them a note or reference that is exactly
a certain number of digits wide - each one hinging on some exact shape of the raw
row rather than anything about the customer, and each form individually uncommon. But they occur right across the customer base, so they
generate a steady trickle of "why is this labeled wrong" tickets and, more
damaging, they poison the spending-category summaries and payee histories that
several downstream features rely on. That combination is why we are treating it
as ship-blocking rather than a backlog item.

## What we need from engineering

The labeling path is fully deterministic and runs offline - hand it the same
transaction and it reproduces the same wrong answer every time - so each of these
is reproducible on demand and can be pinned down exactly. Get the affected forms
labeling and naming correctly again, and do it without disturbing any transaction
that is already labeled right today. A fix that rescues these cases but nudges the
behavior of ordinary, currently-correct transactions is not acceptable: the pass
condition is simply that the specific problem payments described above come out
right and everything else stays exactly where it is.

Research complete. Here is the full report.

## 1. Overall repo structure

**Language/stack:** Python 3.9, Flask REST service (regex + pandas `np.select` rule engine — no ML). Packaged via `setuptools`, deployed via Docker/gunicorn on port 9898.

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                       # python:3.9.2, pip install -e ., gunicorn on :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                     # deps: Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4, fuzzywuzzy, scikit-learn...
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py              # Flask app factory + request timing logger
        ├── Controller.py            # HTTP routes: / , /categorizeTransaction , /recurrentTransactions
        ├── BankScripts/             # 32 per-bank modules (SBI.py, HDFC.py, ICICI.py, Kotak.py, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/          # shared regex constants, helpers, cross-bank enrichment
```

**Pipeline** (per `Controller.py:69` `/categorizeTransaction`): request JSON → `AppUtil.clean_input_df` → bank-specific `categorize_<Bank>_transactions()` (sets `transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory`, `partyName`) → `Purpose.purpose()` → `CleanName.clean_names()` → optional `InternalPayment`, `SalaryDetection`, `PFMCategorization`, `SimpleDescription`. Each bank module follows the same pattern: lists of `[condition, choice]` pairs fed to `np.select`.

## 2. Transaction type classification (with line numbers)

Classification lives in each of the 32 files under `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/` (first `conditions_choices` block sets `transactionCategory`), driven by regexes in `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` and `RegexConstants.py`. Category/subcategory labels are enumerated in `UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` and `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py`.

**Cheque detection**
- `BankScripts/HDFC.py:30,38,50,69–75,100,126` — CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY, STOP_CHEQUE_CHARGES, CHEQUE_CASH_WITHDRAWAL, CHEQUE_RETURN, CHEQUE_PAID/CHEQUE_DEPOSIT (debit/credit split), 16-digit remark → CHEQUE_DEPOSIT, cheque bounce → INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE
- `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py:80–90` (`HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1–10`), `:139–148` (`PNB_CHQ_0–8`), `:262–299` (`FT_CHQ_PATTERN1–37`), `:313–315` (`CHQ_PATTERN1/2`)
- `UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py:86` — `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` regex; applied in `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py:145–147` to split CHEQUE_RETURN into TECHNICAL_BOUNCE vs INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE
- Similar cheque blocks exist in every bank file (e.g. `SBI.py`, `PNB.py`, `Kotak.py`, `ICICI.py`)

**NACH/ACH parsing (AUTO_PAYMENT / AUTO_CREDIT / ECS)**
- `BankScripts/IDBI.py:38` (`\bACH-|Direct Debit|^NACH` → AUTO_PAYMENT); `BankScripts/HDFC.py:51,55` (`^ACH D-`, `^ACH C` etc.); `BankScripts/Kotak.py:44–45` (`^ECSICR|^NACH-...-CR` → AUTO_CREDIT, `^NACH-` debit → AUTO_PAYMENT); `BankScripts/UnionBank.py:40–41`; `BankScripts/PNB.py:37,40`; `BankScripts/SBI.py:48–49`; `BankScripts/StandardCharted.py:59–61`; `BankScripts/IDFC.py:31,35`; `BankScripts/Federal.py:37–38`; `BankScripts/Saraswat.py:34–35`; `BankScripts/SouthIndian.py:37`; `BankScripts/UCO.py:25`; `BankScripts/CityUnion.py:31`; `BankScripts/Citi.py:53`
- ECS bounce penalties: `BankRegexConstants.py:111` (`ECS_PENAL`), `:387` (`ECS_PENAL_YES`); `SBI.py:29`, `Canara.py:25`, `SouthIndian.py:19`, `DCB.py:24`, `UnionBank.py:24`, `Bandhan.py:19`

**Mandate verification / mandate charges**
- AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES: `BankScripts/Kotak.py:39` (`MAND VER CHR` etc.), `Syndicate.py:34` (`MANDATE VER CHG|MNDT:VR:CHG`), `SBI.py:33` (`^ACH MANDATE CHARGE|E mandate`), `PNB.py:14` (`MNDTVRFCHGS`), `UnionBank.py:30` (`MNDVER|EMandate.*Chg`), `ICICI.py:32`, `Federal.py:21` (`^CHRG/NACH MNDTE/`), `Central.py:23,52`, `Canara.py:44`, `IDBI.py:33`, `BankOfMaharashtra.py:39`
- Rupee-1/2 mandate → ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION: `Axis.py:24–26`, `Indusind.py:29–31` (amount==2 + "MANDATE"), `HDFC.py:13`, plus the `BANK_VER*`/`ACC_VERI*` regexes in `BankRegexConstants.py` (e.g. line 75 `BANK_VER_HD`) — every bank file has this at its top (~line 12–14)

**Refund / card (POS) reversal**
- `BankScripts/HDFC.py:19–25` — REFUND, CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL (`^POS.*RVSL|^CRV POS|^POS REF`), UPI_REVERSAL, IMPS_REVERSAL, ATM_REVERSAL, generic REVERSAL; `HDFC.py:98–99` — matched debit/credit pair heuristic → REVERSAL / AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE
- `StandardCharted.py:16–32`; `Syndicate.py:14–22` (POS PUR credit → CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL); `Saraswat.py:12–20` (POSRev); `UnionBank.py:14–18`; `TamilnadMerchantile.py:14–18`; `UCO.py:20–21,36`; `YES.py:25–26,42`; `ICICI.py:18` (REV_NACH → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE)
- Per-bank refund/reversal regex constants: `BankRegexConstants.py:181–182` (VISA_REFUND), `:323,339–355,373–376,391–412` (REVERSAL_/REFUND_ constants for Canara, KarurVyasa, CityUnion, UCO, YES, Federal, RBL); `RegexConstants.py:91` (REFUND), `:103` (TAX_REFUND)
- Downstream normalization: `UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py:73,180–181`; `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py:156–158,173,294`

## 3. Payee/counterparty name extraction

- **Primary extraction** is the `partyName` `conditions_choices` block inside each bank file, e.g.:
  - `BankScripts/HDFC.py:146–275` — NEFT/IMPS/UPI/ACH/cheque splits, e.g. line 169 `^ACH D- BD-NACH-` → `sep_by_dash(desc,3,4)` (exactly the "ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES" style narration)
  - `BankScripts/IDBI.py:81–88` — `^ACH-BD-NACH` → `sep_by_dash(desc,2,3)` etc.
  - `BankScripts/Kotak.py:124–131`, `StandardCharted.py:118–122` (incl. line 122 extracting the name between a 16-digit ref and a 4-letter+14-digit UMRN — the "GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR" style token pattern `[A-z]{4}[0-9]{14}`), `PNB.py:142–143`, `SBI.py:173`, `Canara.py:139`, `YES.py:80,105`, `IDFC.py:71–80`, `Saraswat.py:68`, `SouthIndian.py:63–64`, `Citi.py:114`, `ICICI.py:137–138,166–167`
- **Splitting/extraction helpers:** `UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py:14–66` — `sep_by_` (slash), `sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_wave`, `sep_by_colon`, `sep_by_under`, etc., and `py_extract` (regex extract with NaN handling, line 61)
- **Cross-bank name cleanup:** `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` (`clean_names`, line 9; 1971 lines of merchant/lender canonicalization, e.g. lines 602, 1745–1756 for NACH loan names) and `UtilityScripts/CardCleanNames.py` (`card_clean_names`, line 9) for credit cards
- **Pattern constants** feeding extraction: `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` (432 lines: `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN*`, `FT_PATTERN*`, `FT_CHQ_PATTERN*`, `PNB_CHQ_*`, `SBI_AUTOPAY*`, POS_REFUND_PATTERN line 77, etc.)

## 4. How tests are run

**There are no tests in this repository.** No `tests/` directory, no `test_*.py` files, no pytest/unittest imports, no CI config, and `setup.py` declares no test framework. The only executable entry points are the Flask app (`gunicorn ... categorizationapp:app` per the Dockerfile, or `python __init__.py` dev server on port 9898). Verification would have to be done by POSTing to `/categorizeTransaction`.

## 5. Recent git changes

Only a single commit exists — the entire history is one import:

- `fc21c7f` "import codebase" (Author `t <t@t>`, dated 2026-07-15) — adds all 54 files (11,242 insertions), including every BankScripts and UtilityScripts file listed above.

Working tree is clean (`git status`: nothing to commit), single branch `main`, no stashes, no uncommitted modifications to any of the classification/extraction files.

steps.message:
All five customer-reported defects are reproduced, fixed, and verified. Summary of root causes and fixes (4 lines changed across 3 files):

**1. Cheque filed as "general transfer" (note = cheque number only)**
- `BankScripts/Indusind.py:64` — the remark rule only matched exactly 5 digits (`^[0-9]{5}$`), so a 6-digit cheque number fell through to `TRANSFER`. Every other bank with this rule (Axis:58-59, BankOfMaharashtra:73-74) uses `^[0-9]{5,6}$`. Fixed to `^[0-9]{5,6}$`.

**2. Salary shows "NACH" instead of employer name (`ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES`)**
- `BankScripts/IDBI.py:83` — the `^ACH-BD-NACH` rule took dash-segment 2 ("NACH") instead of segment 3 (the name). Fixed to require the trailing dash (`^ACH-BD-NACH-`) and take `sep_by_dash(3,4)` — mirroring HDFC's equivalent rule (HDFC.py:169). Narrations without the trailing dash still fall to the `^ACH-BD-` rule below and produce the exact same name as before.

**3. Blank sender name on `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`-style transfers**
- `BankScripts/IDBI.py:110` — `py_extract(..., pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)` asked for capture group 1 of a single-group pattern, which always yields empty. Fixed to `index=0`.

**4. ₹1 mandate token confirmation filed as transfer instead of verification**
- `BankScripts/BankOfMaharashtra.py:36-37` — `amount.isin(["1","-1"])` compared strings against a numeric column (`clean_input_df` runs `pd.to_numeric`), so both ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION rules were dead code. Fixed to `isin([1,-1])` / `isin([1])`, matching Axis.py:24/26.

**5. Card refund labeled REFUND instead of CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL, depending on account category**
- `BankScripts/Indusind.py:26` — the reversal rule was gated on `accountType=="SAVINGS"`, a value that never occurs (the API and all 45 other checks use `"SAVING"`), so POS credits ≥ ₹10 always fell to the REFUND rule below. Fixed the typo to `"SAVING"`.

**Verification** (no test suite exists in the repo, so I built one):
- Targeted repro of all 5 tickets: wrong before, correct after.
- 51-row regression matrix across the three touched files (cheques, NACH, NEFT/UPI/IMPS/POS, mandate charges, small-POS refunds, ATM, transfers, both account types): output byte-identical before vs. after, except the five broken forms.
- End-to-end smoke test through the real `/categorizeTransaction` Flask endpoint (full Purpose → CleanName → InternalPayment → SalaryDetection pipeline): all 10 assertions pass. (The `SalaryDetection` scipy traceback in the logs is pre-existing, internally caught at SalaryDetection.py:215, and occurs for any single-credit payload — unrelated to these changes.)
